title: Restriction compatibility of the proper direct-image coefficient comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $Z,Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $p:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism and $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ an open immersion. Put $Z_V=Z\times_YV$, let $u:Z_V\hookrightarrow Z$ be the induced open immersion, and let $p_V:Z_V\to V$ be the projection. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module objects over the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings and the derived operations of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a listed coefficient map in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]: a homomorphism of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, a finite-extension map $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$, localization $\mathcal O_E\to E$, inclusion $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a continuous map $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, or a finite composite of these. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $F/E$ are finite inside a fixed algebraic closure; topological coefficient rings are condensed, with the finite-subextension convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Write $T_T=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ for derived extension of scalars [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], and $\gamma_{p,M}:T_YRp_*M\to Rp_*T_ZM$ for the unit/pullback-comparison/counit morphism of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]. For $M\in\Dctf(Z,\Lambda)$, bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the canonical open-restriction maps are isomorphisms
$$b_{p,M}:v^*Rp_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{V,*}u^*M,$$
over both $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$. Under these isomorphisms and the pullback coefficient identifications $v^*T_Y\simeq T_Vv^*$ and $u^*T_Z\simeq T_{Z_V}u^*$ of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), one has
$$b_{p,T_ZM}\circ v^*(\gamma_{p,M})=\gamma_{p_V,u^*M}\circ T_V(b_{p,M}).$$
The equality is an equality of morphisms from $T_V(v^*Rp_*M)$ to $Rp_{V,*}T_{Z_V}(u^*M)$ after exactly those identifications. Here the canonical open-restriction map is the usual derived exchange map: insert the unit for $p_V^*\dashv Rp_{V,*}$, use $p_V^*v^*\simeq u^*p^*$, and apply the restricted counit for $p^*\dashv Rp_*$; for an identity square it is the identity under the identity-functor identifications.
